forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Mid Devon audit stalled by valid objection to 2025-26 accounts, follows material HRA error
news_drafts.lead: Mid Devon's external auditors cannot issue their audit certificate for 2025-26 after a valid objection to the financial statements was received. The hold-up follows discovery of a material error in the Housing Revenue Account, where internal controls failed to identify that the statement showed net income of £192k when it should have shown net expenditure of £4.7m—a discrepancy of £4.9m. The error, which exceeded the materiality threshold of £1.4m, was corrected in the final accounts presented for audit, but the valid objection now prevents closure. The council's draft Annual Governance Statement notes ten audit recommendations remain overdue, including two high-priority actions, while a Patch Management audit received limited assurance due to three high-impact observations.
news_drafts.paper_title: Mid Devon District Council Audit Completion Report 2025-26 - Version to Audit Committee

findings.headline: Climate change commitments 2030 rated corporate risk 15, with zero EV chargers installed against target 2 in Q1
findings.detail: The council has rated the risk of failing to meet its 2030 climate change commitments as a corporate risk of 15 (on a scale where 20 is highest), with no improvement in the quarter. Electric vehicle charger installation has stalled with zero chargers installed against a target of 2. This indicates progress on stated environmental commitments is at material risk.
findings.matters: Failure to meet stated climate commitments exposes the council to reputational risk and potential future regulatory consequences. For a lender, it signals a gap between stated strategy and delivery capacity, or governance issues in strategy execution.
findings.figures: Corporate risk rating 15 (no change); EV chargers installed 0 vs target 2
findings.quote: Failure to meet Climate Change Commitments by 2030 15 (No change)

findings.headline: Sundry debt recovery performance has fallen to 70.4% of the annual target collection rate.
findings.detail: The council is collecting sundry debts (miscellaneous amounts owed to the council) at 70.4% efficiency against a target of 97.5%. This 27 percentage point shortfall represents material underperformance in collection and creates a direct cash flow risk. Weak debt collection can also signal rising difficulty among the council's debtors.
findings.matters: Weak debt collection directly affects the council's cash flow and may be an early warning sign of deteriorating financial position among the council's debtors, a leading indicator of broader economic stress in the district.

findings.headline: Planning application fee income is forecast to fall £200k short of the annual target.
findings.detail: Statutory planning fees are coming in at £635k against an annual target of £835k, a shortfall of £200k. Discretionary fees are meeting target. The scale of the statutory income shortfall suggests either lower planning application volumes or lower fee-generating activity than forecast.
findings.matters: Planning fee income volatility indicates changes in local development activity or fee-earning planning work. This affects the council's discretionary resources and is a leading indicator of economic activity in the district.
findings.figures: Statutory fees £635k vs £835k target (£200k shortfall); discretionary fees £187k vs £187k target

findings.headline: Service revenue budgets across three major portfolios are projected to overspend by approximately £700k in Q1.
findings.detail: Planning Environment & Sustainability is £180k over, Homes General Fund £50k over, and Service Delivery £475k over. These are not isolated pressures. The pattern of simultaneous overspends across different service areas suggests cost pressures may be structural rather than one-off, raising questions about whether the base budget is sufficient or whether inflationary pressures are outpacing provision.
findings.matters: Multiple simultaneous revenue overspends across different service portfolios indicate systemic cost pressures that may persist and constrain the council's financial flexibility and reserves drawdown.
findings.figures: PE&S overspend £180k (£1,414k vs £1,234k); Homes overspend £50k (£748k vs £698k); SD&CI overspend £475k (£5,046k vs £4,571k)
findings.quote: PE&S PDG – Projected Outturn after EMR £1,414k £1,234k R

findings.headline: Capital project implementation is delayed across all council service areas, with Planning Environment & Sustainability at 75% slippage and HRA capital £12m underspent.
findings.detail: Systematic delays in capital project delivery span multiple portfolios: PE&S at 75%, HRA 47%, Economy & Assets 41%, and Service Delivery 24%. The HRA alone shows £12m underspent on a £25.5m budget. This pattern raises questions about whether the council has realistic project timelines, adequate delivery capacity, or whether external constraints are blocking progress.
findings.matters: Persistent capital slippage across multiple portfolios is a primary indicator of execution risk for a lender considering borrowing facilities. It signals either that capital programmes are mispriced or the council lacks capacity to deploy borrowed funds effectively.
findings.figures: PE&S capital slippage 75% (£70k spent vs £960k budget); HRA capital slippage 47% (£13,510k vs £25,555k); E&A slippage 41%; SD&CI slippage 24%
findings.quote: PE&S PDG – Projected Capital Outturn £70k £960k R

daily_post.headline: Three categories of governance recommendations remain unimplemented after 2–3 years of audit recommendations
daily_post.lead: Persistent failure to implement governance recommendations across multiple audit cycles suggests weak implementation discipline or low prioritisation of soft controls.
